subject: Learning Methods
title: Step One: Choose and Write
description: A fast breakdown of Step One: Choose and Write for builders.

hook.text: Step one of the Feynman technique: write the name of the concept at the top of a blank page. Then explain it below.

buildup.text: Write your explanation as if your reader has zero background. Use examples, analogies, and simple words only.

discovery.text: This step externalizes your understanding. Thoughts that felt clear in your head often turn murky on paper.

twist.text: Most people skip this step because it is uncomfortable. That discomfort is the point. It exposes where knowledge stops.

climax.text: Write for ten minutes without checking any sources. Let the gaps appear naturally. Each gap is a learning target.

punchline.text: Write without notes. Let the gaps show themselves.

quiz.question: Why should you write your Feynman explanation without checking sources?
options: Looking things up takes too much time
It exposes genuine gaps in your understanding
Sources contain errors that could confuse you
